core_obligations: Base case: for d = 0 the positivity follows from the cited lemma on coherent sheaves with zero-dimensional support (proof lines 10587-10588).

Reduce to the case where Z = X is a proper variety: use the intersection-number-in-terms-of-components lemma to assume Z integral, then replace X by Z and each L_i by its restriction to Z (proof lines 10589-10593).

Use additivity of intersection numbers to replace L_1 by a positive tensor power, so that there is a nonzero section s of L_1 whose nonvanishing locus X_s is affine, and note that X is not affine since it is proper of positive dimension (proof lines 10594-10603).

Show the vanishing scheme Z(s) is nonempty: since X is a variety, s is a regular section of L_1, so Z(s) is an effective Cartier divisor of codimension one and hence of dimension d - 1 (proof lines 10604-10611).
Apply the effective-Cartier-divisor intersection lemma to rewrite (L_1 ... L_d . X) as (L_2 ... L_d . Z(s)) and conclude by the induction hypothesis (proof lines 10612-10618).
proof_roadmap: Induct on the dimension, with the zero-dimensional case from finite support.
Reduce to an integral Z equal to X.
Tensor L_1 by a high power to obtain an affine nonvanishing locus and a nonempty divisor of zeros.
Convert the intersection number into one on the divisor and apply induction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that (L_1 ... L_d . Z) is positive when L_1, ..., L_d are ample on a proper scheme X over a field and Z is a closed subscheme of dimension d. The proof inducts on d: the zero-dimensional case follows from the finite-support Euler characteristic lemma, and in the inductive step one reduces to Z integral and then to Z = X a proper variety, replaces L_1 by a positive tensor power so that a section with affine nonvanishing locus exists, observes that X is not affine so the section has a nonempty vanishing scheme Z(s) which is a regular effective Cartier divisor of dimension d - 1, rewrites the intersection number as (L_2 ... L_d . Z(s)) using the effective-Cartier-divisor lemma, and concludes by induction (proof lines 10586-10618). H2: the reduction chain together with the construction of the divisor from a global section is the substance; each step is a specific geometric input, not a citation list.
